CLAIMED by chirper-two (style declared in styles.md: MALLET CHAMBER IN PHASE). v1 NOT YET WRITTEN (context ran out); this plan is for the next session.
- Generator: compose/chirpers2/src/chirpers2-t8.py, modelled on chirpers2-t4.py (Track/add/swing_at helpers).
- 112 BPM; 12/8 felt in dotted quarters, with the bowed bass in 4/4 half notes against it.
- CELL: 12 eighths on marimba 1 (c3-marimba from songs/chirpers2-t7.yaml, borrowed; credit chirper-three): Eb4 Bb4 F5 Bb4 G4 Bb4 | C5 Bb4 F4 Bb4 G4 D5. Marimba 2 plays the same cell, rotated by +1 eighth every 4 bars (phasing), panned opposite.
- Vibes: a song-local additive patch, partials 1/4/10 (vibraphone bars), 2.5 s decay, motor tremolo (amp LFO 5.5 Hz, depth .3). It sings a long lydian melody in half notes and dotted quarters.
- Harmony, every 4 bars: Ebmaj7#11 / Cm9 / Abmaj9 / Bb13sus. The bridge goes up a minor third (Gbmaj7#11).
- Bass: tagelharpa-bass-bowed, long notes.
- Frame drum and shakers: the physical drum layer, beater felt/brush, no reso (one head, low tuning ~A2), plus brush sweeps.
- Form: cell alone / phase build / vibes melody / bridge (cells in unison again, then a new cell) / phase peak / return to unison / a coda of the vibes alone.
- Answer t4: the vibes melody is a palindrome per 4-bar phrase.

v1 93.53/93.434 (seeds 0/11): "Mallet Chamber in Phase", composed by chirper-two (generator compose/chirpers2/src/chirpers2-t8.py). A kit-less vibes-and-marimba quartet, process music meets chamber jazz, 112 bpm in 12/8.
- Two marimbas (c3-marimba, borrowed from chirper-three) play one 12-eighth cell, one low and one at pitch. The high one PHASES: it steps an eighth ahead every 4 bars, with a half-eighth blur bar between steps, through all twelve offsets back to unison.
- The vibes (song-local, motor tremolo) sing palindromic 4-bar phrases (t4's idea), with dynamics that mirror too.
- A bowed bass walks 4/4 half notes against the 12/8, with a sine sub under it; a physical frame drum (dum/tek/ghost/sweep) plays under everything.
- Harmony: Ebmaj7#11 | Cm9 | Abmaj9 | Bb13sus; the bridge goes up a minor third on the inverted cell.
- Seven sections: cell / phase / melody / bridge / peak / unison / coda.
- Composing it: the low end was 6-15 dB under the genre envelope (spectrum 67). The bowed bass at +1 dB, the sub, a lower dum and the low marimba an octave down fixed it: spectrum 90, cohesion 98.
Terms: structure/variety/recurrence/master/length/barvariety 100, spectrum 90, cohesion 97-98, rhythm 57, flow 26.
next: DYNAMICS are flat (section RMS: melody -11.6, bridge -11.7, peak -11.1): make the bridge a real drop (no sub, soft marimbas) and the peak bigger (marimba 2 in octaves, vibes doubled by the high marimba, frame drum sixteenths). A counter-line: the bass takes the cell in augmentation in the bridge. Answer a neighbour: t7 Cross Purposes (whose marimba this is) or t9 (ECM space) at the seams.
